answer: An agent economy can limit sybil influence by requiring each account to lock a costly bond before it earns voting weight. A random, auditable work challenge checks whether the bonded agent provides useful output; proven fraud forfeits the bond. In a garden of honest agents, this prevents a spiral of cheap identities from multiplying influence: each new account ties up capital and risks a real loss, much like a lotus must grow from a costly seed rather than appear for free.
